name: Earned Income Tax Credit
coverage: Screens the tax year 2025 adjusted gross income limits by filing status and number of qualifying children, the investment income limit, and the age rule for claiming without a qualifying child.
limitations: Only tax year 2025 is encoded; a different tax year must be reviewed before it is screened.
Qualifying child relationship, age and residency tests are not applied here.
Citizenship, Social Security number and Form 2555 rules are not checked.
Maximum credit amounts are ceilings published by the IRS, not amounts anyone is guaranteed.
The IRS decides the credit when a return is filed.
eligibilitySummary: The Earned Income Tax Credit lowers the tax owed by people who work and earn a low to moderate income, and can lead to a refund.
Whether you qualify depends on your earned income, your adjusted gross income, your filing status and how many qualifying children you claim.
You can qualify with no children if you were at least 25 and under 65 at the end of the year and meet the other rules.
The IRS makes the final decision when your return is filed.

evidence.text: For tax year 2025 the maximum adjusted gross income is $19,104 with no children ($26,214 married filing jointly), $50,434 with one child ($57,554 jointly), $57,310 with two children ($64,430 jointly) and $61,555 with three or more children ($68,675 jointly).
For tax year 2025 investment income must be $11,950 or less.
For tax year 2025 the maximum amount of the credit is $649 with no qualifying children, $4,328 with one, $7,152 with two and $8,046 with three or more.

To qualify you must have earned income, have investment income below the limit, have a valid Social Security number by the due date of the return including extensions, be a U.S. citizen or resident alien all year, not file Form 2555, and meet certain rules if separated from a spouse and not filing jointly.
Eligible filing statuses are married filing jointly, head of household, qualifying surviving spouse, single and, under specific conditions, married filing separately.

You can claim the credit without a qualifying child if you lived in the United States for more than half the tax year, cannot be claimed as a qualifying child or dependent of another person, and were at least 25 and under 65 at the end of the year; for a joint return at least one spouse must meet the age rule.
The credit has special qualifying rules for military members, clergy members, and taxpayers and their relatives with disabilities.
The IRS publishes an EITC Assistant for checking whether you qualify.
The IRS lists free tax return preparation by trained volunteers and free electronic filing options.
The figures encoded here are the published tax year 2025 amounts; the IRS publishes different amounts for each tax year, so a different year must be reviewed before it is screened.

value.text: For tax year 2025 the published maximum credit is $649 with no qualifying children and up to $8,046 with three or more. These are ceilings, not amounts you are guaranteed.
